summary:
South Australia stands under the Australian national framework: federal law, federal courts and national entry rules apply here and are carried by the national assessment. The findings below are the state's own.

State anti-discrimination law protects gender identity and sexual orientation. The Equal Opportunity Act 1984 was amended in 2016 to add both grounds, giving trans residents and visitors a state-level remedy alongside the federal one.

Hate-crime sentencing laws that explicitly cover sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex characteristics passed and were implemented in November 2021, so offences motivated by a victim's gender identity fall within the state's sentencing aggravation provisions.

The gay-panic defence was abolished on 1 December 2020 and ceased to operate on 1 April 2021. A defendant can no longer rely on a claimed non-heterosexual advance by the victim as a partial defence.

The Conversion Practices Prohibition Act 2024 is in legal effect from 1 April 2025, prohibiting conversion practices in the state.

Birth certificate changes have been available since 23 May 2017 under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration (Gender Identity) Amendment Act 2016, which received royal assent on 15 December 2016. A change of sex descriptor requires appropriate clinical treatment but not sex-reassignment surgery, and a marriage does not have to be ended first. Non-binary and indeterminate sex descriptors are also available on state birth certificates.

Registered domestic relationships have been available since 1 August 2017. Marriage is recognised under the federal Act that took effect in December 2017; 62.5% of South Australian respondents voted Yes in the 2017 postal survey.
tangentialFactors: South Australia was the first Australian jurisdiction to decriminalise male homosexual activity, with the change commencing on 2 October 1975. Its 2016 birth-certificate reform placed it, with the ACT, among the first two jurisdictions to allow a change of the sex recorded on a birth certificate without sex-reassignment surgery.
localsOnly:
The state's scheme for historical gay convictions is spent rather than expunged, under the Spent Convictions (Decriminalised Offences) Amendment Act 2013, in force from 22 December 2013; it is the only such scheme in the country framed that way.

Same-sex couples have been able to adopt in South Australia since 17 February 2017.
outOfScopeNotes:
A Queensland Human Rights Commission news item on that state's discrimination reforms could not be retrieved (HTTP 403). It concerns another jurisdiction's law and no South Australian finding rests on it.

Sources differ on when the Conversion Practices Prohibition Act 2024 passed, giving September 2024 and October 2024; both give commencement on 1 April 2025.

No South Australian enforcement data for the November 2021 hate-crime sentencing provisions was located, so their practical application is not documented in the sources reviewed.

Federal sex-discrimination law and the national court precedent interpreting it apply in South Australia; the national assessment carries them and they are not restated here.
